record.paper_title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
record.original_question: Given a continuous bounded function g on \mathbb{R}_+, do there exist continuous functions b, k_0, and k_1 such that every solution of u(t) = g(t) + b(t)u(qt) + \int_0^t k_0(t-s)u(s)\,ds + \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)u(s)\,ds is asymptotically stable, meaning \lim_{t	o\infty} u(t)=0?

evidence.quote: Open Problem 4.1 (a) (ii) If g is as in (1), are there continuous functions b, k0 and k1 so that the solutions of u(t) = g(t)+b(t)u(qt)+∫ t 0 k0(t−s)u(s)ds ∫ qt 0 k1(t−s)u(s)ds, t \ge 0, (4.7) satisfy (4.2)?

artifact.category_tag: Volterra functional equations with proportional delay
artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix a constant $q \in (0,1)$. Let $g : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ be a given continuous, bounded function. Determine whether there exist continuous functions $b, k_0, k_1 : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ (in the case of $k_0$ and $k_1$, viewed as kernels on the appropriate domain) such that every continuous solution $u : \mathbb{R}_+ \to \mathbb{R}$ of the Volterra functional integral equation with vanishing (proportional) delay
$$u(t) \;=\; g(t) \;+\; b(t)\, u(qt) \;+\; \int_0^t k_0(t-s)\, u(s)\, ds \;+\; \int_0^{qt} k_1(t-s)\, u(s)\, ds, \qquad t \ge 0,$$
is asymptotically stable in the sense that
$$\lim_{t \to \infty} u(t) \;=\; 0.$$
Either exhibit such functions $b, k_0, k_1$ (with explicit conditions on $g$ guaranteeing the property), or prove that no such triple exists.
artifact.status_search_result: The question is posed as an open problem on the existence of stabilizing coefficient and kernel functions for a Volterra integral equation with proportional (vanishing) delay. A search did not produce a published resolution of this specific stability question.

status_evidence.title: Current work and open problems in the numerical analysis of Volterra functional equations with vanishing delays
status_evidence.snippet: Listed as Open Problem 4.1 concerning asymptotic stability of solutions of a Volterra equation with proportional delay.
status_evidence.claim: The question is presented as an unresolved open problem.
